newsitem.title: UK: UK GILTS END VOLATILE DAY NEARLY HALF POINT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: UK GILTS END VOLATILE DAY NEARLY HALF POINT DOWN.

text.p: 1520 GMT - UK gilts end choppy day nearly half a point down on volatility in U.S. Treasuries and weakness in stg. Market edged up earlier on strong fall in UK unemployment and BOE inflation report.
British unemployment for July tumbled by 49,800, but June average earnings remained static at 4.25 percent.

The Bank of England's quarterly inflation report and a statement from the Bank confirming that interest rates are on hold for the time being also brought some relief to the gilts market, but not enough to resist the downward thrust of Treasuries.
But analysts also said the Bank's announcement of a brake on rates hit sterling and this weakness persisted during the day, conspiring to drag gilts lower.
"We're down on Treasuries and sterling," said Stephen Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking.

"This (sterling weakness) combined with the rapid turnaround in U.S. Treasuries which indicated the lack of retail buyers in that market led to the loss of all the earlier gains...and really we're looking quite soggy at the moment."
The 10-year gilt/Bund spread held steady at 151 basis points and analysts said it was likely to hover around this area fro the foreseeable future.
The short sterling strip was discounting interest rates of at least 7.25 percent by the end of the year. The September short sterling contract was unchanged on the day at 92.78.
